derivation: Read committed x70view translation units and disassemble the actual overlay with arm-none-eabi-objdump -D -b binary -m arm --adjust-vma=0x01100000. NONMATCHING C and donor names are not treated as target behavior.

roots.claim: BSS1 schedule header bytes3,4..5,6,7; count<=8; each 16-byte row copies flags/count and three full little-endian words. Aggregate flags OR header flags with every row flag. Then rebuild the BSS beacon. The draft C incorrectly suggests a byte load for the second row word; actual 0x012fc228 is a full word load.
The direct body begins with BSS index1 and has six bytes. Mode2 stores bytes1..5 into BSS fields0x100,0x104,0x108,0x10c,0x1a7 before the peer fold. Other modes leave state unchanged.

Active mode2 folds allocated associated BSS1 peers. PHY mask0x1a controls nonERP, PHY0x10 and HTbit1 select protection0/2/3, HTbit4 controls nongreenfield, capability0x20/0x400 reduce preamble/slot, HT0x4000 and BSS flags0x1a6/0x1a7 suppress secondary-offset publication. A changed projection enqueues CMD1d before beacon CMD1c; the RX root forces beacon refresh even if unchanged.
Requires mode0. Connection state0 publishes disconnect reason4, then tears down the selected peer if present. The shared RX dispatcher owns adapterdef1==0 admission.

reachable_helpers.claim: Sixteen-byte BSS body for CMD1d, including trailing0x72. Band/channel/configured offset precede peer projection, HT words, advertised offset/preamble/slot.
CMD1c update mode1, BSS1, capability u16 at body4, IE length u16 at body6, IE bytes at body8. Reject IE lengths greater than600. Adapter owns command header and sequence.

Uses the existing beacon descriptor when present; builds ordinary SSID/rate/channel/TIM elements and invokes the ordered element producers at0x012e16c4 before CMD1c. The clean CPU reuses the AP-produced element stream and projects dynamic ERP/HT/OBSS fields into it rather than invoking stock callbacks.

ERP uses root byte1, nonERP and short preamble. HT operation advertises channel, effective secondary offset, protection with root byte2==1 precedence except legacy protection3, nongreenfield bit2, HT info3, then sixteen zero basic-MCS bytes.
BSS1 HT mode2 on band1 with configured secondary offset appends OBSS element74 with seven u16 parameters20,10,300,200,20,5,25.
The null-profile abort branch calls the disconnect publication path with reason4 and no optional body.
The reached arg2=0 branch transitions the peer to state0, clears secondary session fields, sets disconnected BSS state1, enqueues changed interface CMD16, then nonAP CMD1b and HT reset.

Associated peer downgrade cancels its hardware receive/reorder queues. Authenticated->disconnected is local-only; other reached transitions publish shared CMD17 body40. Canonical PeerPool and Association IBSS provider own these shared operations.
Changed interface publication serializes80 bytes for CMD16, preserving the selected peer index and embedding the BSS16-byte body at offset64.
CMD1b carries a four-byte BSS1 body.

Resets HT/root projections and clears coexistence channel lists, cancels the coexistence timer at BSS0x18c, and clears20/40MHz flags. The runtime clears its timer ownership and root after successful flush completion.

redesign: Physical command bodies are retained across errors. No implicit resend or success is synthesized. Explicit retry re-exposes the same immutable body.
The shared peer generation is retained through teardown and released only after the final physical flush completion.
The source halt preconditions become typed parse/admission errors; unknown body extents are not read.
AP security, rates and vendor element production stay with the canonical AP and association providers. This module owns secondary projection, not a second authenticator, peer allocator or transport.
